headline: Rogers Beats on Sports Revenue as Wireless Remains Sluggish
author: Stephanie Hughes

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- Rogers Communications Inc. beat analyst earnings expectations on gains from sports assets, but the company's core wireless business is still struggling to find growth.
Canada's biggest mobile phone provider earned C$1.29 per share on an adjusted basis in the third quarter, more than the C$1.23 average estimate in a Bloomberg survey of analysts.

Rogers' media revenue rose to C$821 million, up 9% from a year ago. The company doubled its stake in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment last year, and as of Oct. 1, it owns 100% of the company that runs the Toronto Raptors basketball club and Toronto Maple Leafs hockey team.

Rogers already owned Major League Baseball's Toronto Blue Jays and it plans to sell a minority stake in a consolidated sports, media and entertainment company, targeting a deal in the first half of 2027.

"The close of the MLSE transaction marks a significant milestone in our plan to unlock shareholder value from our sports and media assets, which continue to show global breadth and scale," Chief Executive Officer Tony Staffieri said in a statement.

Revenue in the wireless segment, Rogers' largest business, was C$2.69 billion, up 1% from a year ago. The company added just 6,000 net postpaid mobile subscribers during the quarter, less than the roughly 33,000 expected by analysts. A year ago, it added 62,000.
Adjusted Ebitda was up 1% from last year's third quarter in both the cable and wireless divisions. Ebitda is earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.

Temporary foreign workers and international student visas have been restricted in Canada under an immigration tightening that began in 2024, limiting the pool of new users. Telecom firms had been using aggressive discounts to encourage customers to switch providers.
